requirements.requirement: Daily 02:15 cron job configured on node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance
requirements.summary: Root crontab was updated to include '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' alongside pre-existing periodic entries, confirmed directly via crontab -l both before and after a full node reboot, showing the entry persists.

requirements.requirement: crond must actually run and be enabled so the schedule fires (necessary prerequisite for the above)
requirements.summary: crond was found stopped at discovery; executor added it to the default OpenRC runlevel and started it. Post-reboot check confirms crond auto-started and remains enabled in the default runlevel.

The exact cron command was manually invoked (both before and after the reboot) and its output was shown appended to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, with prior content preserved across the run and across the reboot, directly demonstrating the append pipeline works as configured.

requirements.requirement: /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance must be a working, executable script (necessary for the schedule to produce meaningful output)
requirements.summary: Discovery showed the script as shipped (644, non-executable) contained literal leftover heredoc/setup text rather than valid script content — a pre-existing defect, not executor-caused. The executor rewrote it to a correct #!/bin/sh script, set 0755 root:root, and confirmed correct output both immediately and after reboot.

overall_summary: The task's two material outcomes — a daily 02:15 cron entry for /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and retention of its output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log — are both directly satisfied with pre- and post-reboot evidence. The maintenance script was discovered broken (a pre-existing prepare-stage defect, not executor-introduced) and was correctly repaired as a necessary step to make the schedule meaningful. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: a healthy pre-restart baseline, a genuine reboot (boot_id changed from 67b90295... to 2b72ecd9..., with an observed connection reset during the transition), and full post-restart recovery of crond, the cron entry, the script, and the log content, plus a fresh successful run confirming the pipeline still functions.
limitations: The scheduled 02:15 firing itself was not observed live (only manual invocations of the identical command were captured); this is expected given the bounded evidence window and is not treated as a gap in the cron configuration or crond enablement, both of which were directly verified.
Package-health and failed-services checks are unsupported/unremarkable on this Alpine image and add no further signal beyond what is cited.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: fixing the pre-existing broken script (necessary prerequisite), installing/enabling the cron entry and crond service (core task), manual test runs (bounded evidence collection for the log-append pipeline), and the reboot plus its verification commands (provider-wide restart-evidence protocol). No troubleshooting dead-ends or unrelated mutations were observed. One minor residue: the backgrounded reboot command created /tmp/reboot.log (cmd-93ff9e1ba4b94e0f), visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot and not cleaned up — a small, low-risk leftover file rather than anything destructive or security-weakening.
